title.zh: 卷377 列傳一百六十四 鲍桂星 顾莼 吴孝铭 陈鸿 鄂木顺额 徐法绩
title.en: Volume 377 Biographies 164: Bao Guixing, Gu Chun, Wu Xiaoming, Chen Hong, E Mushune, Xu Faji
title.raw: 卷377 列傳一百六十四 鲍桂星 顾莼 吴孝铭 陈鸿 鄂木顺额 徐法绩

sentences.zh: 列傳一百六十四

translations.literal: Biographies, Number 164
translations.idiomatic: Biography 164

sentences.zh: 鮑桂星顧吳孝銘陳鴻鄂木順額徐法績

translations.literal: Bao Guixing, Gu Chun, Wu Xiaoming, Chen Hong, E Mushune, and Xu Faji
translations.idiomatic: Bao Guixing, Gu Chun, Wu Xiaoming, Chen Hong, E Mushune, and Xu Faji

sentences.zh: 鮑桂星，字雙五，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Bao Guixing, style name Shuangwu, was a man of She County, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Guixing, whose courtesy name was Shuangwu, came from She County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，遷中允。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was promoted to vice-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fourth year of the Jiaqing reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, became a compiler, and rose to vice-director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九年，典試河南，留學政。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he served as chief examiner for Henan and remained behind as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he presided over the Henan provincial examination and stayed on as educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十三年，典試江西。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he served as chief examiner for Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 十五年，督湖北學政。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he supervised education in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was appointed educational commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 累遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 十八年，任滿，既受代，聞林清之變，疏陳十事，急馳至京，仁宗嘉之，曰：「汝所奏已次第施行矣。」

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when his term ended and he had already handed over office, he heard of the Lin Qing incident, memorialized ten matters in a memorial, and hurried to the capital; the Renzong Emperor praised him, saying, "What you memorialized has already been carried out in order."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, as soon as his term ended and he had handed over his post, he learned of Lin Qing's uprising. He submitted a memorial outlining ten measures and rushed to the capital. Emperor Renzong praised him, saying, "The items you raised are already being implemented, one after another."

sentences.zh: 擢工部侍郎，充武英殿總裁。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Works and made chief director of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Works and appointed chief director of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 桂星性質直，勇於任事。

translations.literal: Guixing's nature was upright and blunt, and he was bold in taking on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guixing was blunt and upright by nature, and bold in shouldering responsibility.

sentences.zh: 十九年，疏陳刊書及校勘事宜。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he memorialized on the publication of books and matters of collation and proofreading.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he submitted a memorial on book publishing and textual collation.

sentences.zh: 又劾提調劉榮​​黼等不職，命王大臣按之。

translations.literal: He also impeached the supervising officials Liu Rongdian and others for dereliction of duty, and the emperor ordered a princely minister to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached supervising officials including Liu Rongdian for neglect of duty, and the throne ordered a senior prince-minister to conduct an inquiry.

sentences.zh: 榮黼面訐桂星曾言滿總裁熙昌所校，不過偏旁點畫，修改徒延時日；

translations.literal: Rongdian confronted Guixing face to face, charging that Guixing had once said that what the Manchu chief director Xi Chang had collated amounted only to radicals and dots and strokes, and that the revisions merely prolonged the days;
translations.idiomatic: Rongdian confronted Guixing in person, alleging that Guixing had once said the Manchu chief director Xi Chang's collation work amounted to nothing more than tweaking radicals and stroke dots, needlessly dragging out the schedule;

sentences.zh: 且言近日有旨，旗人不足恃，故督撫多用漢人。

translations.literal: and he also said that recently there had been an edict that Bannermen could not be relied upon, so governors-general and governors increasingly employed Han Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: and further claimed that a recent edict had declared Bannermen unreliable, so that governors-general and governors were increasingly appointing Han Chinese.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，怒，命傳詢。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he grew angry and ordered the matter transmitted for inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it, grew furious, and ordered the matter referred for investigation.

sentences.zh: 桂星對聞自侍郎周兆基，且言在部與滿員共事，多有徇私背公，而兆基不承；

translations.literal: Guixing replied that he had heard it from vice minister Zhou Zhaoji, and also said that in the ministry, when working with Manchu colleagues, there was much favoritism contrary to the public good, yet Zhaoji would not admit it;
translations.idiomatic: Guixing answered that he had heard it from Vice Minister Zhou Zhaoji, adding that in the ministry he had often seen Manchu colleagues indulge private favor at public expense, which Zhaoji denied;

sentences.zh: 又指同官熙昌及慶溥囑託部事，兩人亦不承。

translations.literal: he also named colleagues Xi Chang and Qing Pu as having solicited favors in ministry affairs, and neither of the two would admit it.
translations.idiomatic: he also accused colleagues Xi Chang and Qing Pu of soliciting favors in ministry business, and both denied it.

sentences.zh: 以任性妄言，下部嚴議，詔斥桂星指訐慶溥、熙昌囑託無據，其咎小；

translations.literal: Because of willful reckless speech, the case was sent down to the ministry for severe deliberation; an edict rebuked Guixing: accusing Qing Pu and Xi Chang of solicitation was without evidence—the fault was small;
translations.idiomatic: For reckless and willful speech the case was sent to the ministry for severe deliberation. An edict rebuked Guixing: his charge that Qing Pu and Xi Chang had solicited favors lacked proof and was a lesser offense;

sentences.zh: 妄言朝廷輕滿洲重漢人，亂政之大者：革職，不准回籍，令在京閉門思過，責五城御史嚴察；

translations.literal: recklessly saying that the court slighted Manchus and favored Han Chinese was a great matter of disordering government: he was dismissed from office, not permitted to return to his native place, ordered to remain in the capital behind closed doors to reflect on his faults, and the Five-City censors were charged to watch him strictly;
translations.idiomatic: but claiming the court slighted Manchus while favoring Han Chinese was a grave offense against good government. He was stripped of office, forbidden to return home, ordered to remain in Beijing under house arrest to reflect on his conduct, with the Five-City censors instructed to keep strict watch;

sentences.zh: 如私著詩文有怨望誹謗之詞，從重治罪。

translations.literal: if in private writings of poetry or prose there were words of resentment, discontent, or slander, he was to be punished severely.
translations.idiomatic: and if any private poetry or prose he composed contained resentment or slander, he was to be punished severely.

sentences.zh: 越五年，上意解，复官編修。

translations.literal: Five years later the emperor's anger eased, and his office as compiler was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later, when the emperor's anger had cooled, Guixing was restored to his former post as compiler.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，召對，諭曰：「汝昔所劾，今已罷斥。」

translations.literal: When the Daoguang Emperor took the throne, Guixing was summoned for audience; the emperor instructed him, saying, "Those you impeached in the past have now been dismissed."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daoguang ascended the throne, Guixing was summoned for an audience. The emperor told him, "The men you impeached back then have now been removed from office."

sentences.zh: 擢侍講，又擢通政司副使，意頗鄉用。

translations.literal: He was promoted to expositor-in-waiting, then again to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and the court seemed inclined to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to expositor-in-waiting and then to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission, and the court appeared ready to make greater use of him.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，擢詹事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daoguang he was promoted to Supervisor of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he died.

sentences.zh: 桂星少從同縣吳定學，後師姚鼐，詩古文並有法，著有進奉文及詩集，又嘗用司空圖說輯唐詩品。

translations.literal: In his youth Guixing studied under Wu Ding of the same county, and later took Yao Nai as his teacher; his poetry and ancient-style prose were both methodical. He authored memorial essays presented to the throne and a collection of poems, and he also once compiled Tang poetry grades according to Sikong Tu's theory.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Guixing studied under his fellow townsman Wu Ding and later studied under Yao Nai. Both his poetry and his ancient-style prose were accomplished by rule. He wrote memorial essays for presentation at court and a poetry collection, and he once compiled grades of Tang poetry according to Sikong Tu's critical theory.

sentences.zh: 顧蓴，字南雅，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Gu Chun, style name Nanya, was a man of Wu County, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Chun, whose courtesy name was Nanya, came from Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the seventh year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 十七年，大考一等，擢侍讀。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, in the great triennial evaluation he ranked first class and was promoted to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he ranked in the top class in the great triennial evaluation and was promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 督雲南學政，道經河南，見吏多貪墨，奸民充斥，密疏陳謂不早根治，恐釀巨患。

translations.literal: While supervising education in Yunnan, passing through Henan he saw that many officials were corrupt and that wicked commoners filled the province; in a secret memorial he stated that if this were not rooted out early, it might breed a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: On his way to serve as educational commissioner of Yunnan he passed through Henan and found officials widely corrupt and rascals thick on the ground. In a confidential memorial he warned that failure to eradicate the problem early could breed disaster on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 仁宗問樞臣，樞臣微其事，不以為意，明​​年遂有滑縣之亂。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor asked the Grand Council, but the council minimized the matter and paid it no heed; the next year the Huaxian uprising broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong consulted the Grand Council, but the council downplayed the report and took no notice. The following year the Huaxian rebellion erupted.

sentences.zh: 在雲南，課士嚴而有恩，以正心術端行誼為首，次治經史、辨文體。

translations.literal: In Yunnan he instructed scholars strictly yet with kindness, putting rectification of mind and integrity of conduct first, and next the study of classics and histories and discrimination of literary forms.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan he taught the scholars with strict standards tempered by kindness, giving first place to moral discipline and upright conduct, and next to classical learning, historical study, and mastery of literary form.

sentences.zh: 按試所至，聞賢士必禮遇之，士風丕振。

translations.literal: Wherever he went on inspection tours, if he heard of worthy scholars he invariably treated them with courtesy, and scholarly custom was greatly revived.
translations.idiomatic: On his inspection tours he always honored worthy scholars when he heard of them, and local scholarly morale rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 任滿，充日講官。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was appointed lecturer at the daily lectures.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was appointed to the daily lecture service at court.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，遷侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was transferred to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 值宣宗初政，疏請停捐例。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daoguang Emperor's new rule he memorialized requesting suspension of the sale of offices by contribution.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Daoguang's reign he memorialized asking that the sale of offices through monetary contributions be halted.

sentences.zh: 再疏陳崇君德、正人心、飭官方三事。

translations.literal: In a second memorial he set forth three matters: exalting the ruler's virtue, rectifying the people's hearts, and tightening official discipline.
translations.idiomatic: In a second memorial he urged three reforms: strengthening the ruler's moral authority, rectifying public sentiment, and tightening official conduct.

sentences.zh: 上召對，嘉納其言。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience and commended and accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him for an audience and warmly accepted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 故事，大臣子弟不得充軍機章京，時值考選，許一體與試。

translations.literal: By precedent, sons and younger brothers of great ministers could not serve as clerks in the Grand Council; at that time an examination for selection was under way, and they were permitted to compete on equal terms.
translations.idiomatic: By longstanding rule, sons and younger brothers of senior ministers were barred from the Grand Council clerkships; but when examinations for selection were held at that time, they were allowed to compete on equal footing.

sentences.zh: 蓴謂貴介不宜與聞樞要，請收回成命。

translations.literal: Chun said that men of high birth ought not to be privy to matters of state secrecy, and requested that the approved order be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Chun argued that men of privileged birth should not be admitted to confidential state business and asked that the concession be revoked.

sentences.zh: 事尋止。

translations.literal: The matter was soon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The policy was soon abandoned.

sentences.zh: 左都御史松筠出為熱河都統，蓴上疏，謂松筠正人，宜留置左右，失上意，降編修，九歲不調。

translations.literal: When Left Censor-in-Chief Songyun was sent out as commander of Rehe, Chun memorialized, saying Songyun was an upright man and ought to be kept at the emperor's side; he lost imperial favor, was demoted to compiler, and for nine years received no transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When Left Censor-in-Chief Songyun was posted out as commander of Rehe, Chun memorialized that Songyun was a man of integrity who should be kept close to the throne. The memorial displeased the emperor; Chun was demoted to compiler and went nine years without a new appointment.

sentences.zh: 先是嘉慶中蓴在史館，撰和珅傳，及進禦，經他人竄改，和珅曾數因事被高宗詰責，並未載入傳。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Jiaqing period, while Chun was in the Historiography Office he drafted the biography of Heshen; when it was presented to the throne it had been tampered with by others. Heshen had several times been rebuked by the Gaozong Emperor for various matters, yet none of this was entered in the biography.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Jiaqing reign, Chun had been in the Historiography Office and drafted Heshen's biography. By the time it reached the throne others had altered it, omitting the many occasions on which Emperor Gaozong had censured Heshen for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 仁宗怒其失實，嚴詔詰問。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor was angry at its lack of truth and issued a stern edict demanding explanation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong, angered by the distortion, issued a stern edict demanding an account.

sentences.zh: 大臣以蓴原稿進，仁宗深是之，而奪竄改者官。

translations.literal: The great ministers submitted Chun's original draft; the Renzong Emperor deeply approved it, and stripped the tamperers of office.
translations.idiomatic: Senior ministers submitted Chun's original draft. Emperor Renzong strongly endorsed it and dismissed the officials who had altered the text.

sentences.zh: 宣宗一日閱實錄至此事，嘉蓴直筆，因言前保留松筠，必非阿私，特擢蓴右中允。

translations.literal: One day the Daoguang Emperor, reading the Veritable Records, came upon this affair and praised Chun's honest brush; he said that Chun's earlier effort to retain Songyun could not have been private flattery, and specially promoted Chun to right vice-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: One day Emperor Daoguang, reading the Veritable Records, came upon the episode and praised Chun's honest historiography. Saying that Chun's earlier defense of Songyun could not have been sycophancy, he specially promoted Chun to right vice-director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未一歲，复侍講學士原職。

translations.literal: In less than a year he was restored to his former post as expositor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he was restored to his former rank as expositor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 時回疆張格爾亂甫定，蓴疏：「請於喀什噶爾沿邊增重兵，以控制安集延，杜回人窺伺；

translations.literal: At that time the Zhang Ge'er rebellion in the Muslim borderlands had just been pacified; Chun memorialized: "I request that along the borders of Kashgar heavy troops be added to control Andijan and block Muslim reconnaissance;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Zhang Ge'er rebellion in the Western Regions had only just been suppressed. Chun memorialized: "Along the Kashgar frontier additional troops should be stationed to control Andijan and forestall Muslim probing;

sentences.zh: 又其地密邇英吉沙爾、葉爾羌、和闐，皆有水草可耕牧，宜募民屯田，為戰守備。

translations.literal: moreover, that region lies close to Yengisar, Yarkand, and Khotan, all of which have water and pasture suitable for farming and herding; commoners should be recruited to open military colonies as provisions for war and defense.
translations.idiomatic: moreover the region borders Yengisar, Yarkand, and Khotan, where water and pasture support farming and grazing. Civilians should be recruited for frontier settlement to supply both defense and garrison needs.

sentences.zh: 更請慎選大臣，無分滿、漢，務得讀書知大體有方略者任之，而以廉靜明信能拊循民、回者為之佐，庶可永永無事。」

translations.literal: I further request that great ministers be chosen with care, without distinction between Manchu and Han, striving to obtain men who have read books, understand the larger pattern, and possess strategy to hold the post, while as assistants men who are incorrupt, tranquil, trustworthy, and able to stroke and guide Han and Muslim peoples—then perhaps there may be peace without end."
translations.idiomatic: He further urged that frontier governors be chosen with care from both Manchu and Han ranks—men of learning who grasp the larger strategic picture—and that they be assisted by officials who were upright, steady, trustworthy, and able to win over both Han settlers and Muslim communities. Only then, he argued, could the border remain permanently quiet."

sentences.zh: 道光十一年，遷通政司副使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Daoguang he was transferred to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Daoguang he was promoted to vice commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 湖南北、江南、江西、浙江大水，蓴疏言：「饑民與鹽梟糾合易生事，鹽梟不盡去，終為巨患。

translations.literal: Great floods struck Hunan, Hubei, Jiangnan, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang; Chun memorialized, saying: "Starving people joining with salt smugglers easily gives rise to trouble; if salt smugglers are not wholly removed, in the end they become a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When severe floods hit Hunan, Hubei, the lower Yangzi, Jiangxi, and Zhejiang, Chun memorialized: "Hungry refugees who ally with salt smugglers can quickly turn violent. Unless smuggling rings are broken up, they will become a lasting scourge.

sentences.zh: 緩治之則養禍深，急治之則召禍速，欲禁其妄行，必先謀其生路。

translations.literal: To treat the problem slowly nurtures a deep calamity; to treat it urgently summons swift calamity. If one wishes to forbid their reckless actions, one must first plan a livelihood for them.
translations.idiomatic: Delay invites a deeper disaster; haste provokes an immediate one. To stop lawless conduct you must first secure lawful livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 現兩淮鹽場漂沒，三江、兩湖勢必仰給蘆、粵之鹽，宜聽民往販，隨時納課，收課後，不問所之，俟鹽產盛，丁力紓，即令課歸丁，不限疆域。」

translations.literal: At present the salt fields of Liang Huai have been inundated; the Three Rivers region and the two lake provinces will necessarily depend on salt from Lu and Guangdong. It is fitting to allow the people to go and trade, paying duty as they go; after duty is collected, do not inquire where the salt goes. Wait until salt production flourishes and the salt laborers are relieved, then let the duty return to the laborers and do not limit the territory."
translations.idiomatic: With the Huai saltworks flooded, the Yangzi delta and the lake provinces would have to rely on salt from the reed-boil and Guangdong trades. He proposed allowing free private transport with duties paid en route, no questions asked after collection, and—once production recovered and transport costs eased—shifting tax burdens back onto producers without confining trade by region."

sentences.zh: 事下所司，格未行。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the responsible offices, but the regulations blocked it and it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was referred to the relevant agencies, but existing regulations blocked it and nothing was implemented.

sentences.zh: 蓴性嚴正，尚氣節，晚益負時望，從遊者眾，類能砥勵自立，滇士尤歸之，其秀異者至京師多就問業焉。

translations.literal: Chun's nature was stern and upright; he prized integrity; in his later years he bore ever greater public esteem. Those who studied under him were many, and for the most part they could sharpen themselves and stand on their own. Yunnan scholars especially looked to him; their outstanding men, on reaching the capital, often came to seek instruction from him.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was stern and upright, devoted to moral principle. In later life his reputation only grew, and a large circle of disciples learned self-discipline under him. Yunnan scholars revered him above all; their most talented men, once in Beijing, often sought him out for guidance.

sentences.zh: 十三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 吳孝銘，字伯新，江蘇陽湖人。

translations.literal: Wu Xiaoming, style name Boxin, was a man of Yanghu, Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiaoming, whose courtesy name was Boxin, came from Yanghu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十四年進士，選庶吉士，散館授工部主事，充軍機章京。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and upon leaving the academy was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Works and served as a Grand Council clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and on leaving the academy was appointed principal clerk in the Ministry of Works and then clerk in the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 十八年，林清之亂甫定，大軍會攻滑縣，孝銘從大臣行，參軍事。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, when the Lin Qing uprising had just been pacified, the great army converged to attack Huaxian; Xiaoming accompanied the great ministers on the campaign and took part in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, just after Lin Qing's rebellion was suppressed, imperial forces converged on Huaxian. Xiaoming accompanied the commanding ministers and assisted in military planning.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to the rank of director.

sentences.zh: 道光中，回疆用兵，首逆張格爾潛逋未獲，議者欲以克復四城，分封回部酋長。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang period, when troops were used in the Muslim borderlands, the chief rebel Zhang Ge'er remained at large uncaptured; some advisers wished to enfeoff Muslim tribal chiefs by dividing the four recovered cities among them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign, as campaigns continued in the Western Regions, the rebel leader Zhang Ge'er was still at large. Some officials proposed enfeoffing Muslim chieftains by parceling out the four recovered cities among them.

sentences.zh: 孝銘密言於樞臣曰：「是可行於乾隆時，不可行於今日，行之邊患且益甚。」

translations.literal: Xiaoming said privately to the Grand Council: "This could be done in the Qianlong period; it cannot be done today. If done, border troubles will grow worse still."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoming told the Grand Council privately, "That might have worked in the Qianlong era, but not today. Carry it out and the frontier crisis will only deepen."

sentences.zh: 議中止。

translations.literal: The proposal was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 張格爾旋就俘，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Zhang Ge'er was soon captured, and Xiaoming was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ge'er was captured soon afterward, and Xiaoming was awarded the peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 瀕年大水，江、浙、兩湖被災尤數，承回疆兵事後，度支大絀。

translations.literal: Near the end of his life great floods occurred; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and the two lake provinces suffered disaster especially often. This came after the border campaigns in the Muslim regions, and state revenue was severely strained.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year there were great floods; Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and the lake provinces suffered especially often. Coming on the heels of the Western Region campaigns, the treasury was severely depleted.

sentences.zh: 戶部擬議，宗室日以蕃衍，衣食悉仰之官，耗財之大者，請自係出世祖以上子孫皆改為覺羅，為覺羅者以次遞革。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue drafted a proposal: imperial clansmen daily multiplied, and food and clothing all depended on official provision—a great drain on finances. It requested that from descendants of the Shizu on upward all be changed to jueluo status, and that those made jueluo be reduced in rank in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue drafted a plan noting that the imperial clan was expanding daily while its members depended entirely on state stipends—a major fiscal drain. It proposed reclassifying all descendants of the Shizu Emperor and earlier as jueluo, with each new jueluo generation subject to successive reductions in rank and allowance.

sentences.zh: 孝銘曰：「茲事當密陳，不宜顯言。

translations.literal: Xiaoming said: "This matter ought to be reported confidentially; it should not be stated openly.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoming said, "This should be raised in confidence, not proclaimed openly.

sentences.zh: 法當緩更，不宜驟易。

translations.literal: The method ought to be changed slowly; it should not be altered abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Reform should proceed gradually, not all at once.

sentences.zh: 宗室久受恩養，一旦降爵減糧令下即大困，因而呼籥，朝廷不得已，將必復之，是良法美意終於不行也。」

translations.literal: The imperial clan has long received imperial nurture; once an order lowering rank and reducing grain allotments is issued they will at once be greatly distressed, and thus will cry out in appeal; the court will have no choice but to restore them—so a good law and fine intention will in the end not be carried out."
translations.idiomatic: The clan has grown accustomed to imperial favor. The moment you cut ranks and rations they will be plunged into hardship and flood the court with petitions. Beijing will have no choice but to roll the policy back—so even a sound measure will never take hold."

sentences.zh: 部臣是其言，即使草奏上之。

translations.literal: The ministry officials approved his words and had him draft the memorial to present it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry officials accepted his advice and had him draft the memorial for submission.

sentences.zh: 歷鴻臚寺少卿、光祿寺少卿、通政司參議、順天府丞，仍留直軍機處。

translations.literal: He served in succession as vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, councillor of the Office of Transmission, and vice prefect of Shuntian Prefecture, while remaining on duty in the Grand Council.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, councillor of the Office of Transmission, and vice prefect of Shuntian, all while retaining his Grand Council post.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢太僕寺卿，再遷宗人府丞。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and again transferred to vice minister of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to minister of the Imperial Stud and soon afterward to vice minister of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 孝銘前後在樞廷二十馀年，練於掌故，持議悉合機宜；

translations.literal: Xiaoming served in the Council for more than twenty years, was practiced in precedent, and his proposals all accorded with the opportune moment;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoming spent more than twenty years in the Grand Council, mastered institutional precedent, and framed proposals that consistently matched the moment;

sentences.zh: 屢膺文衡，有公明稱。

translations.literal: he repeatedly undertook literary examinations and had a reputation for fairness and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: he presided over literary examinations many times and was known for impartial judgment.

sentences.zh: 母憂，以毀致疾，服闋，至京。

translations.literal: During mourning for his mother he fell ill from grief; when mourning ended he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he fell ill from grief. When mourning ended he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋乞病歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Soon he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home, dying at his residence.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned on grounds of illness, returned home, and died there.

sentences.zh: 陳鴻，字午橋，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Chen Hong, style name Wuqiao, was a man of Qiantang, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hong, whose courtesy name was Wuqiao, came from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十四年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the fourteenth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 遷御史，剛直有聲。

translations.literal: He was transferred to censor and had a reputation for blunt uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and gained renown for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 典試山西還，力陳驛站煩擾，請申定例，肅郵政。

translations.literal: Returning from serving as chief examiner in Shanxi, he forcefully memorialized on the vexation of courier stations, requesting clarification and enforcement of the regulations to rectify the postal service.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his Shanxi examination assignment he forcefully memorialized on abuses at courier stations, asking that regulations be clarified and enforced to restore the postal system.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，疏陳浙江水利，略曰：「杭城地當省會，用上下兩塘之水，溉仁和、錢塘、海寧之田數万馀頃。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized on Zhejiang water conservancy, stating in summary: "Hangzhou, as the seat of the provincial capital, uses the waters of the upper and lower ponds to irrigate tens of thousands of qing of fields in Renhe, Qiantang, and Haining.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he memorialized on Zhejiang waterworks, writing in part: "Hangzhou, seat of the provincial capital, relies on the upper and lower reservoir systems to irrigate tens of thousands of qing of farmland in Renhe, Qiantang, and Haining.

sentences.zh: 源出西湖，近廢不治。

translations.literal: The source issues from West Lake, which in recent times has been abandoned and not maintained.
translations.idiomatic: The source is West Lake, which in recent years has been neglected and left unrepaired.

sentences.zh: 水淤葑積，塘河津耗，夏旱少雨，上塘枯涸，菑害尤劇。

translations.literal: Water silted up and duckweed accumulated; pond rivers and sluices were depleted; in summer droughts with little rain the upper pond dried up, and crop damage was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Silt and duckweed choked the channels; pond rivers and sluice gates fell into ruin. In summer droughts the upper reservoirs ran dry and crop losses were especially severe.

sentences.zh: 海寧長安鎮號產米之鄉，許村黃灣場為產鹽之地，杭、嘉、湖、寧、紹諸郡賴是挽運。

translations.literal: Chang'an Town in Haining was famed as a rice-producing district; Huangwan Salt Field at Xucun was a salt-producing place on which Hang, Jia, Hu, Ning, and Shao prefectures relied for transport and haulage.
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an in Haining was renowned for grain; the Huangwan salt works at Xucun supplied salt transport on which Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, Ningbo, and Shaoxing all depended.

sentences.zh: 擬請仿江蘇浚吳淞例，歸民間按畝出貲，並飭疆臣躬履屬境，凡堤塘徬壩，悉復舊制，俾農田旱潦有備。」

translations.literal: It is proposed to follow the Jiangsu precedent of dredging the Wusong River, having the people contribute funds by the mu of land, and also ordering frontier officials in person to traverse their jurisdictions; wherever dikes, ponds, and embankments exist, all old systems should be restored, so that farmland may be prepared against drought and flood."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed following Jiangsu's Wusong dredging model, funding repairs through local contributions assessed by acreage, and requiring provincial officials to inspect their territories in person. Every dike, pond, and embankment should be restored to its former standard so that fields would be secure against both drought and flood."

sentences.zh: 又請：「北省多闢水田，兼收秔稻之利，庶使畿輔為沃野，無凶年。」

translations.literal: He also requested: "In the northern provinces many fields should be opened to paddy, jointly reaping the profit of both indica and japonica rice, so that the capital region may become fertile fields without years of famine."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged opening more paddy fields in the north to capture the benefits of both long- and short-grain rice, turning the capital region into rich farmland free of famine years."

sentences.zh: 皆被採納。

translations.literal: All were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were adopted.

sentences.zh: 道光初年，疏陳浙鹺不綱，請裁鹽政，歸巡撫兼理，令整頓緝私，嚴禁掣規重斤科派供應諸弊，如議行。

translations.literal: In the early Daoguang period he memorialized that Zhejiang salt administration lacked unified control, requesting abolition of the salt commissioner, return of management to the governor's concurrent charge, and orders to rectify suppression of smuggling and strictly forbid such abuses as skimming rules, overweight levies, and supply exactions; it was carried out as proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daoguang he memorialized that Zhejiang's salt monopoly was poorly coordinated, proposing abolition of the salt commissioner's office, placing oversight under the governor, and a crackdown on smuggling together with abuses such as rule-bending, overweight charges, and illicit levies for supplies. The reforms were enacted as he proposed.

sentences.zh: 糾劾工部弊竇最多，不避權貴。

translations.literal: He impeached the Ministry of Works, where malpractices were most numerous, and did not avoid the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the Ministry of Works, where corruption was rife, without sparing the powerful.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 二年，奉命稽察銀庫，其妻固賢明，曰：「今而後可送妾輩歸矣！」

translations.literal: In the second year he was ordered to inspect the silver vault; his wife, who was by nature worthy and clear-minded, said, "From now on you may send your concubines back!"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was ordered to audit the silver vault. His wife, a woman of notable sense, said, "From this day forward you may send your concubines home!"

sentences.zh: 驚問之，曰：「銀庫美差也，苟為所染，暱君者麕至。

translations.literal: Startled, he asked why; she said, "The silver vault is a fine appointment; if you are stained by it, those close to you will flock in.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, he asked why. She replied, "The silver vault is a lucrative post. Once you are compromised, flatterers will swarm in.

sentences.zh: 禍且不測，妾不忍見君菜市也。」

translations.literal: Calamity will then be beyond reckoning; your wife cannot bear to see you on the execution ground."
translations.idiomatic: Disaster will follow—and I cannot bear to see you led to the execution ground."

sentences.zh: 鴻指天自誓，禁絕賂遺。

translations.literal: Hong pointed to Heaven and swore, forbidding all bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Hong swore an oath to Heaven and refused all gifts.

sentences.zh: 中庭已列花數盆，急揮去，墮地盆碎，中有藏鏹，益聳懼。

translations.literal: Several flower pots had already been set out in the central courtyard; he hurriedly had them removed; they fell to the ground and the pots shattered, and hidden silver was found within—he was all the more alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Flower pots had already been placed in the courtyard. He ordered them removed at once; they fell and broke, revealing concealed silver inside. His fear only deepened.

sentences.zh: 遂奏庫衡年久鐵陷，請敕工部選精鐵易之。

translations.literal: He then memorialized that the vault's scales, after many years, had iron sunk into them, and requested that the Ministry of Works select fine iron to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized that the vault scales, worn over many years, had iron sunk into them, and asked the Ministry of Works to supply new iron of superior quality.

sentences.zh: 送庫日，責成管庫大臣率科道庫員較驗，然後啟用。

translations.literal: On the day the scales were delivered to the vault, he charged the minister in charge of the vault to lead the censors and clerks in comparison and verification before they were put into use.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the new scales were delivered, he required the vault minister to lead censors and clerks in joint verification before they were placed in service.

sentences.zh: 禁挪壓餉銀、空白出納及劈鞘諸弊。

translations.literal: He forbade the abuses of diverting and withholding pay silver, blank receipts for receipts and disbursements, and splitting ingot sheaths.
translations.idiomatic: He banned diverting troop-pay silver, keeping blank ledgers for receipts and disbursements, and shaving silver from ingot sheaths.

sentences.zh: 庫吏百計餂之，不動。

translations.literal: Vault clerks used a hundred schemes to entice him; he did not move.
translations.idiomatic: Vault clerks tried every trick to win him over, but he would not budge.

sentences.zh: 復請戶部逐月移送收銀總簿，別立放銀簿，鈐用印信，以資考覈。

translations.literal: He further requested that the Ministry of Revenue each month transfer the general ledger of silver received, separately establish a ledger of silver disbursed, affix seals, to supply material for audit.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked the Ministry of Revenue to forward the master receipt ledger each month, keep a separate disbursement ledger, and require official seals on both to enable auditing.

sentences.zh: 先是御史趙佩湘馭吏嚴，其死也，論者疑其中毒。

translations.literal: Earlier the censor Zhao Peixiang had controlled clerks strictly; when he died, those who discussed the matter suspected he had been poisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Censor Zhao Peixiang had ruled the clerks with an iron hand. After his death, many suspected he had been poisoned.

sentences.zh: 鴻蒞庫，勺水不敢飲。

translations.literal: When Hong took charge of the vault, he dared not drink a spoonful of water.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong took charge of the vault, he would not drink even a spoonful of water offered there.

sentences.zh: 出督雲南學政，奏革陋規，嚴束書吏，弊風頓革。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise Yunnan education, memorialized to abolish vulgar regulations, strictly bound clerks, and corrupt practices were suddenly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as Yunnan educational commissioner, he memorialized to abolish entrenched abuses, tightened control over clerks, and corrupt practices were quickly rooted out.

sentences.zh: 遷通政司參議，卒於官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Transmission Office and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner of the Transmission Office and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 鄂木順額，字复亭，鈕祜祿氏，滿洲正藍旗人。

translations.literal: E Mushune, style name Futing, of the Niohuru clan, was a man of the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.
translations.idiomatic: E Mushune, whose courtesy name was Futing, belonged to the Niohuru clan and came from the Manchu Plain Blue Banner.

sentences.zh: 父明安泰，江蘇按察使。

translations.literal: His father Ming Antai was Jiangsu surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ming Antai had served as surveillance commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 鄂木順額，嘉慶二十五年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，累遷右庶子。

translations.literal: E Mushune, in the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, was appointed compiler, and was promoted in succession to right vice-director of the Supervisorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: E Mushune earned his jinshi degree in the twenty-fifth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, became a compiler, and rose in succession to right vice-director of the Supervisorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 道光四年，大考一等，擢翰林院侍講學士，遷少詹事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daoguang, in the grand examination he placed first class, was promoted to Hanlin expositor, and was transferred to junior commissioner of the Supervisorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daoguang he ranked first class in the grand examination, was promoted to Hanlin expositor, and became junior commissioner of the Supervisorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 扈從東巡，命分視御道，內監前驅者多率意馳踐，鄂木順額執而鞭之，則愬於御前。

translations.literal: Accompanying the eastern tour, he was ordered to inspect the imperial road in sections; many eunuch outriders rode willfully and trampled it. E Mushune seized and whipped them, and they complained before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the eastern tour he was assigned to inspect sections of the imperial road. Many eunuch outriders rode recklessly and trampled it. E Mushune seized and whipped them, and they appealed to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 召問，鄂木順額對曰：「關外地與關內異，先驅蹂踐則路壞，慮驚乘輿。

translations.literal: Summoned and questioned, E Mushune replied: "Land beyond the passes differs from within the passes. If outriders trample and tread, the road will be ruined, and I fear startling the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Called in and questioned, E Mushune answered: "The terrain beyond the passes is not like that within them. If outriders trample the road it will be ruined, and I feared alarming the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 且御道非大駕不得行，臣不敢不執法。」

translations.literal: Moreover the imperial road may not be traveled except by the great procession; your servant dared not fail to enforce the law."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, only the imperial procession may use the imperial road. I dared not fail to enforce the law."

sentences.zh: 上韙之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his conduct.

sentences.zh: 命為湖南學政，以在母憂，引禮力辭。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hunan educational commissioner; as he was in mourning for his mother, he cited ritual and forcefully declined.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed educational commissioner of Hunan, but as he was in mourning for his mother he cited ritual propriety and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 服闋，督安徽學政，遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he supervised Anhui education and was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he served as educational commissioner of Anhui and was promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十一年，大雨江溢，學政駐當塗，鄂木順額捐廉以賑，督守令勸捐，士民踴躍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year great rain caused the river to overflow; the educational commissioner was stationed at Dangtu. E Mushune donated his official salary for relief, supervised prefects and magistrates to encourage donations, and gentry and commoners leaped forward eagerly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year heavy rains flooded the river. The educational commissioner was stationed at Dangtu. E Mushune donated his official salary for relief, urged prefects and magistrates to solicit contributions, and gentry and commoners responded enthusiastically.

sentences.zh: 知縣趙汝和盡心民事，而戇直忤大吏，調為鄉試同考官。

translations.literal: Magistrate Zhao Ruhe devoted himself to the people's affairs, but his blunt uprightness offended great officials, and he was transferred to be associate examiner for the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate Zhao Ruhe devoted himself to local affairs, but his blunt integrity offended senior officials, and he was transferred to serve as associate examiner for the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 鄂木順額堅留治賑，事得辦，後上聞。

translations.literal: E Mushune firmly retained him for relief work; the matter was accomplished, and later it was reported above.
translations.idiomatic: E Mushune insisted on keeping him for relief work. The effort succeeded, and the matter was later reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 宣宗以為賢，期滿留任，遷大理寺卿。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong regarded him as worthy; when his term ended he was retained in office and was transferred to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong judged him worthy. When his term ended he was kept in post and promoted to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十二年，鄉試，往江寧考錄遺才，卒於試院。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, during the provincial examination, he went to Jiangning to examine and record overlooked talent and died in the examination compound.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, while presiding over the provincial examination at Jiangning to select overlooked talent, he died in the examination compound.

sentences.zh: 鄂木順額以氣節自勵，在滿洲京僚中稱最。

translations.literal: E Mushune took moral fortitude as his discipline; among Manchu capital officials he was called the foremost.
translations.idiomatic: E Mushune disciplined himself by moral integrity and was regarded as foremost among Manchu officials in the capital.

sentences.zh: 大學士松筠尤重之，曰：「君光明挺直，行且大用，原自愛。」

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Songyun especially valued him, saying: "You are bright, upright, and straight; soon you will be greatly employed—please take care of yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Songyun held him in special regard and said, "You are bright and upright. You will soon be greatly employed—please take care of yourself."

sentences.zh: 為英和門下士，在翰林，非有故不通謁。

translations.literal: He was a disciple of Yinghe; in the Hanlin, without a special reason he did not pay calls.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a disciple of Yinghe. In the Hanlin Academy he paid calls on no one without a proper reason.

sentences.zh: 及英和謫戍，獨送至數十里外。

translations.literal: When Yinghe was banished to border garrison, he alone escorted him several tens of li beyond.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinghe was banished to the frontier, he alone escorted him several tens of li on his way.

sentences.zh: 英和太息曰：「吾愧不知人，平日何曾好待君耶？」

translations.literal: Yinghe sighed deeply and said: "I am ashamed that I did not know men—how ever did I treat you well in ordinary times?"
translations.idiomatic: Yinghe sighed deeply and said, "I am ashamed that I failed to know a man of worth. How often did I ever treat you well in ordinary times?"

sentences.zh: 嘗謁掌院學士玉麟，閽人弗為通，怒叱曰：「英相國獲罪，即若曹為之，奈何猶不知儆！」

translations.literal: Once he called on Academician-in-Chief Yulin; the gatekeeper would not announce him. He angrily shouted: "Grand Councilor Ying was condemned—that was because of your kind! Why do you still not know to take warning!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he called on Academician-in-Chief Yulin, but the gatekeeper refused to announce him. He shouted in anger, "Grand Councilor Ying was condemned—and your sort brought it about! Why have you still not learned to take warning!"

sentences.zh: 翼日，玉麟自往謝。

translations.literal: The next day Yulin went in person to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yulin went in person to apologize.

sentences.zh: 徐法績，字熙庵，陝西涇陽人。

translations.literal: Xu Faji, style name Xi'an, was a man of Jingyang, Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Faji, whose courtesy name was Xi'an, came from Jingyang in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶二十二年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in the twenty-second year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 以親老歸養，家居十年。

translations.literal: Because his parents were aged he returned home to support them and lived at home ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When his parents grew old he returned home to care for them and remained there ten years.

sentences.zh: 道光九年，遷御史，謂諫臣當識大體，不宜毛舉細故瀆上聽，致久浸生厭。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Daoguang he was transferred to censor and said that remonstrating officials ought to grasp the larger pattern, should not pick petty matters and weary the emperor's ear, lest long immersion produce disgust.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Daoguang he was promoted to censor. He argued that remonstrating officials should grasp the larger pattern, not weary the throne with petty complaints, lest constant triviality breed contempt.

sentences.zh: 疏陳求人才、捐文法、重守令、繩貪墨四事。

translations.literal: In a memorial he set forth four matters: seeking talent, setting aside formalistic law, emphasizing prefects and magistrates, and restraining the corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on four measures: recruiting talent, easing formalistic regulations, strengthening prefects and magistrates, and punishing corruption.

sentences.zh: 會直隸、河南地震成災，劾罷監司不職者二人。

translations.literal: At the time earthquakes in Zhili and Henan became disasters; he impeached and dismissed two incompetent surveillance and circuit officials.
translations.idiomatic: When earthquakes struck Zhili and Henan and brought disaster, he impeached and removed two incompetent provincial supervisors.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，稽察銀庫，無所染。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretary, inspected the silver vault, and was stained by nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to supervising secretary, audited the silver vault, and remained uncorrupted.

sentences.zh: 十二年，分校會試，同官與吏乘隙為奸，匿雲南餉銀，法績出闈亟按之，謀始沮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he served as divisional examiner for the metropolitan examination; colleagues and clerks seized an opening for knavery and concealed Yunnan pay silver. Faji left the examination compound and immediately investigated; the plot was finally thwarted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, while serving as divisional examiner for the metropolitan examination, colleagues and clerks seized an opening for fraud and concealed Yunnan pay silver. Faji left the examination compound and investigated at once, and the plot was thwarted.

sentences.zh: 典試湖南，其副病歿，獨專校閱，遍搜遺卷，拔取多知名士，而得於遺卷者六人，大學士左宗棠其首也。

translations.literal: He presided over the Hunan examination; his deputy died of illness. He alone specialized in examination reading, searched leftover papers everywhere, and selected many famous scholars. Six were obtained from leftover papers, Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang being the first.
translations.idiomatic: He presided over the Hunan provincial examination. When his deputy died of illness he undertook the reading alone, searched every leftover paper, and selected many men who later became famous. Six were found among the rejected papers, foremost among them Grand Secretary Zuo Zongtang.

sentences.zh: 以薦赴東河，學習河工，週曆兩岸，詳詢利弊，著錄為東河要略一篇。

translations.literal: On recommendation he went to the Eastern River, studied river works, toured both banks in circuit, inquired minutely into advantages and harms, and wrote it down as one piece entitled Essentials of the Eastern River.
translations.idiomatic: On recommendation he went to the Eastern River conservancy, studied hydraulic engineering, toured both banks, investigated advantages and drawbacks in detail, and recorded his findings in a monograph entitled Essentials of the Eastern River.

sentences.zh: 十四年，遷太常寺少卿。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 尋以病乞歸，逾二年卒。

translations.literal: Soon he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home; after more than two years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned on grounds of illness and returned home, dying a little more than two years later.

sentences.zh: 論曰：鮑桂星、顧蓴以鯁直獲譴，卒見諒於明主，蓴之建白，尤卓卓矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Bao Guixing and Gu Chun were punished for blunt uprightness, yet in the end were understood by a clear sovereign; Chun's proposals were especially outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Bao Guixing and Gu Chun were punished for blunt integrity, yet in the end won understanding from an enlightened sovereign. Chun's proposals were especially outstanding.

sentences.zh: 吳孝銘通達政體，鄂木順額樸誠持正，陳鴻、徐法績清操相繼，冀挽頹風，而庫藏大獄，卒發於十數年之間，甚矣實心除弊之罕覯其人也！

translations.literal: Wu Xiaoming mastered government forms; E Mushune was plain and honest in uprightness; Chen Hong and Xu Faji's integrity succeeded one another—they hoped to reverse declining winds—but the great vault cases finally broke out within a dozen or so years. How rare are those who earnestly remove abuses!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiaoming mastered the workings of government; E Mushune was plainspoken, sincere, and upright; Chen Hong and Xu Faji upheld integrity in succession, hoping to reverse a declining age. Yet the great vault scandals finally erupted within a dozen years. How seldom does one meet a man who earnestly sets out to root out abuses!
